quote: Well, actually, I don't want it for the home. I want it for a garage.
stewart_read: The call opens on a mismatch between the lead record (home) and what the customer actually wants (a detached, newly-built, unmetered garage). No schema section addresses garage-only or unmetered-structure requests — this is a genuine gap in Ion's script coverage, not a rep error. The rep adapts smoothly rather than trying to force the standard homeowner flow.
alternative_hypothesis: A reactive read would fault the rep for not immediately flagging the mismatch as a scope question — but the transcript shows the rep pivoting its verify questions to the garage context within seconds, which supports the adaptive read over a failure read.
coaching_implication: Flag for Kenny as a schema gap: does Ion's install program even support solar for an unmetered accessory structure, and if so, what's the qualifying question set? This is a floor-wide question, not a rep-specific coaching item.

stewart_read: The garage has no separate meter, which is a material fact for how solar would even be metered/net-metered for that structure. The rep acknowledges it ('No problem at all') and moves on without probing whether this is a hard blocker, likely because that determination sits with the specialist's site visit.
alternative_hypothesis: A stricter read would say the rep should have asked the utility company's rules on sub-metering or shared-meter solar; but nothing in the current schema equips a setter to make that call, so deferring to the specialist visit is the reasonable path given the tools the rep has.
coaching_implication: Not a rep-level fix — surface to Kenny that setters need a decision rule for unmetered secondary-structure requests: is this an automatic route to specialist, or should it be screened out at setter stage?

quote: Then do you know the square footage of that garage?
stewart_read: The rep collects a raw number (26 by 26, roughly 400-500 sq ft) but doesn't reflect it back as a forward-pulling hook (e.g., tying the size to what the specialist could realistically cover). The data is filed, not used to build anticipation for tomorrow's visit.
alternative_hypothesis: Given the call's short, transactional shape and the customer's own uncertainty about the number ('I don't know what the square footage you have to add up'), the rep's neutral acknowledgment may be the efficient choice rather than a miss — pushing for more precision here risks bogging down an already scope-limited setter call.
coaching_implication: Minor — model for the rep a one-line bridge such as 'that'll give the specialist a great starting point for sizing tomorrow' to connect the data point to the upcoming visit without overselling.

quote: So can you just can you give me a consensus of what it would take to have that minimal amount of solar up there?
stewart_read: This is a price/ballpark ask, similar in shape to the script's price_estimate_before_design trigger. Larry is asking for a 'minimal amount' framing — a soft cost-consciousness signal — but the rep doesn't reflect back any bill-pain or savings angle since no bill was ever discussed (this is a garage load, not a home bill).
alternative_hypothesis: Because this call never established a home bill anchor (the customer explicitly wants solar for a garage, not the home), there is no bill pain to invert against — the objection_inversion mechanism doesn't cleanly apply here, and rebuttals.price_estimate_before_design fits better.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to use the rebuttals.price_estimate_before_design language ('cost depends on roof, shading, usage — let's get you real numbers, not a ballpark') rather than the flatter scheduling-department disclaimer actually used.

quote: So I'm not too sure only because I'm in the scheduling, and design department.
stewart_read: This is actually the rep correctly HOLDING scope rather than creeping — the rep declines to estimate cost/sizing and defers to the specialist visit. Tagged here as the positive counter-example to scope creep: the rep does not volunteer premature pricing or technical sizing content.
alternative_hypothesis: A critical read might say the deferral sounds unpolished ('I'm not too sure') rather than confident — but the underlying strategy (redirect to specialist) matches the schema's universal escape hatch.
coaching_implication: Reinforce this as the right instinct; coach delivery polish only — replace 'I'm not too sure' with something closer to the schema's suggested phrasing: 'that's exactly what my specialist will walk you through tomorrow' to sound more confident while keeping the same scope discipline.

quote: So if that's a concern of yours, I can go ahead and put it down here in our notes to make sure my specialist goes over it with you.
stewart_read: The rep offers to flag the cost question for the specialist, but conditionally ('if that's a concern of yours') — it is not confirmed whether Larry actually wants this noted, and the transcript doesn't show an explicit yes from him.
alternative_hypothesis: This could be read as adequate handoff practice since the rep offers to document it; but because Larry never explicitly confirms he wants it noted, this is better framed as a soft, unconfirmed commitment rather than a locked promise.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to close the loop explicitly — ask 'want me to have him prioritize that?' and get a yes/no, so the handoff note reflects a confirmed customer request, not an assumed one.

quote: Is it a brand new garage that you just built? Yes. Yes. We just had it built this week.
stewart_read: A brand-new, two-story garage built this week is a strong positive signal — new construction means no legacy wiring constraints and an engaged, recently-invested homeowner. No schema section currently captures 'new construction' as an enthusiasm trigger, but it functions the same way trees-removed or EV-purchase signals do in the existing enthusiasm framework.
coaching_implication: Flag for Kenny as a candidate addition to the enthusiasm-signal catalog: recent/planned construction on the property. In the moment, the rep could have leaned into this ('great timing since it's all fresh construction') to build rapport, but simply moved to the next verify item.

stewart_read: The rep never runs the explicit 'is that fair?' handshake or the no-driving/computer instruction from button_up before ending the call — the close is friendly but procedurally thin, resting on 'we'll shoot you a text' rather than a locked verbal confirmation.
alternative_hypothesis: Because this is an in-person specialist visit rather than a phone appointment, the no-driving/computer language may not apply directly — but the missing 'is that fair?' handshake is still a gap regardless of channel.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to add the verbal handshake ('does 12 o'clock tomorrow work for you — is that fair?') even on in-person bookings; it's a two-second addition that locks the commitment before hanging up.
